identity.trade: Furs and ravens: the last village before Grimfen Pass, where trappers watch the snowline and ravens watch the trappers.

greeting: I am the headman. Nobody voted. Nobody objected.
Looking for something? I know a man who knows where it is.
rumour: The law is far, the pass is near, and I am in between.
The watch does not come past the third post after dark. That is the arrangement.
On clear winter nights the north sky goes green and the ravens go quiet.

opinions.rulf_middleton: Rulf works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Early. Sleep is for the respectable.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
Welcome to Ravenscar. Mind the Ravenscar Raven Tower. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Nobody signs the book. I stopped asking years ago. The rooms are never empty.
Travellers say the stones are dimmer on the east road. I water the ale, not the news.
A pedlar lost his pack and found it two days later, repacked and slightly lighter.
Trappers found bones bigger than a cart below the ridge. Horned, and frosted.

opinions.brida_ingleby: Brida is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.evening: Dusk. The good hours start now.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
Strangers in Ravenscar get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: I make locks and I make keys. I do not ask who the keys are for.
Good steel is dear. Bad steel is dearer, the day it breaks.
A man in grey asked about a debt older than he is. We sent him to the ravens.

opinions.rook_dunmow: I would trust Rook with a purse. A small one.

time.night: Night. Business is brisk. Mind your pockets.

dialogue.aside: Sit. I have news. Three pieces, one of them true, I think.

greeting: Take your time. Touch nothing you cannot afford.
You did not see me. I did not see you. Lovely.
rumour: Locks are the one thing I do not stock. Customers find that funny.
Candles are short this month. The wax comes late, and so does the honest news.
The ravens have learned some people's faces. They avoid the same ones.
Whatever you hear about Ravenscar, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.osric_middleton: Osric is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.rain: Rain covers footprints. A blessing for some of us.

dialogue.aside: Look what the wind dragged in. Sit. Do not touch the pie.

greeting: Papers, if you have them. A good story, if you do not.
Ravenscar is trappers below the pass. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Nine spears for the whole wall. I count them like sheep.
Whoever sells the best pelts in the pass has never been seen to hunt.
The Pass has been shut since the Long Dark. Snow is the lock, and spring is the key.

opinions.lanny_wakeley: Lanny knows the trade. I will say that for Lanny.

time.morning: Early. Sleep is for the respectable.

dialogue.aside: Welcome, welcome. Your name is right there. On the tip of my tongue.

greeting: Halt. Ah. Not a thief. Carry on.
You will hear Ravenscar before you see it. Ask at the Ravenscar Raven Tower.
rumour: Cold on the wall these nights. Colder than the season has a right to be.
A debt was forgiven last week. That is how we know someone is dead.

opinions.lanny_wakeley: Lanny works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Dusk. The good hours start now.

dialogue.aside: A bright day and a bright friend! What luck!

greeting: Evening. Stones are lit, gate is shut, I am cold.
Folk come to Ravenscar for trappers below the pass. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: A stone by the gate flickered at midnight. I wrote it down. Nobody reads it.
A very good lock was sold here last week, and a very good lockpick the day after. Coincidence, say the sellers.

opinions.otto_keld: Otto knows the trade. I will say that for Otto.
opinions.rolf_slater: Rolf works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Night. Business is brisk. Mind your pockets.

dialogue.aside: There you are. I was just thinking of you, which is rare, and a compliment.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
Quiet streets are a gift. Do not spoil them.
rumour: The old stones had names. Nobody writes them down. Nobody asks me.
Fewer guards on the pass this month. More folk who do not want to be seen.
Ravenscar lives by trappers below the pass. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.kendra_nimble: Kendra works hard and talks harder.
opinions.nial_fletcher: Nial keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.rain: Rain covers footprints. A blessing for some of us.

dialogue.aside: Up before dawn, friend? Then you saw the best of the day. I saw it first.

greeting: No names, no receipts, no problems.
First time in Ravenscar? The Ravenscar Raven Tower is the place to start.
rumour: Somebody is buying roads. Not owning them. Buying their silence.
Someone paid in old coin, very old. The face on it was not a king we know.

opinions.dane_plover: Dane knows the trade. I will say that for Dane.
opinions.rulf_middleton: Rulf lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.morning: Early. Sleep is for the respectable.

dialogue.aside: Whatever you need, friend. Ask. I will not make you ask twice.

greeting: Mind the snare by the gate. It is not for you.
Ravenscar is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: A trapper went north in autumn and came back without his dogs.
A cart passed in the night with the lantern covered. Nobody asked what was in it.
Ask anyone in Ravenscar about the Ravenscar Raven Tower. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.nial_fletcher: Nial works hard and talks harder.
opinions.silas_eastman: Silas keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Dusk. The good hours start now.

dialogue.aside: No fear when you are here. Or little. Or I hide it better.

greeting: Feed them first. Then ask. They are fair.
The Ravenscar Raven Tower is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: The ravens circled the pass all night. They never do that. Something was walking.
A stranger asked at the Ravenscar Raven Tower for the oldest person in Ravenscar. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.dane_plover: Dane keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.nial_fletcher: Nial works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Night. Business is brisk. Mind your pockets.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: I saw a light in the hedge last night. Do not tell Mum.
A man in grey asked about a debt older than he is. We sent him to the ravens.

opinions.ansel_hawker: I would trust Ansel with a purse. A small one.
opinions.rulf_middleton: Rulf is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

clues.note: Prints too big for a dog, heading for the tree line.
A dragged carcass. Teeth marks, not knife marks.
The lock is clean and oiled. A lock picked well looks better than one that is not.

stashes.say: You wrap two jars of lamp oil in straw.
